content:
Security researchers have shown that Claude Cowork can escape the sandbox meant to contain its access to your Mac. The flaw, named ShareRoot, could allow attackers to read and write files stored anywhere on your Mac, as well as obtain login credentials for online services.

Collaborative sessions belonging to roughly half a million Mac users have been exposed, and some users remain affected by the flaw to this day…

Claude Cowork allows the AI chatbot to locally access designated files and folders on your Mac so that it can perform tasks on your behalf.

Anthropic provides two layers of protection to prevent the bot from running amok or being exploited by an attacker. First, Cowork runs inside a virtual machine that acts as a sandbox. Second, it can only access the files and folders you explicitly authorise. However, The Hacker News reports that security researchers have found a way to bypass both layers of protection.

Cybersecurity researchers discovered a sandbox-escape vulnerability in Anthropic's Claude Cowork that could allow the agent to break out of the confines of the Linux virtual machine (VM) it runs in, and read or write files anywhere on the Mac. Accomplish AI shared details of the flaw with The Hacker News ahead of publication and said that, until it is fixed, roughly 500,000 macOS users running local Cowork sessions are affected. The vulnerability is codenamed SharedRoot.

With just a brief message, the session could be granted unrestricted read/write access to files anywhere on the Mac, all without the user ever seeing a permission prompt

Although Anthropic has responded, TNW reports that some users remain at risk.

This news story also previously disclosed an OpenAI agent that likewise escaped its sandbox and breached Hugging Face's servers.
